summary: Published src/content/blog/beginner/rascettes-palmistry.md, the next outstanding scored backlog article, drafted only from the Director-verified evidence boundary at .ai-ops/evidence/PP-RELAY-058-benham-rascettes-boundary.md (William G. Benham, The Laws of Scientific Hand Reading, 1900). The backlog's older West (1998)/Fincham (2005) planning note was explicitly out of scope and was not used. The article covers where Benham places the Rascettes at the wrist, his first-bracelet constitution reading, his ambition reading for upward branches, and states both halves of the older thirty-year-per-bracelet lifespan method: it is a real historical claim from the tradition Benham describes, and Benham himself says he could not confirm it and did not use it as a longevity measure. A dedicated 'Palmistry Path's approach' section keeps that historical material clearly separate from the site's own editorial position that wrist creases do not diagnose health, vitality, or predict lifespan, including an in-article medical-guidance note per the style guide. No combination reading with the life line, mounts, travel lines, or hand type was introduced; no West/Fincham or other unverified source was cited; no prevalence/consensus, count-norm, or vague-authority claim was introduced. Added one purely navigational reciprocal link into minor-lines-overview.md's existing 'a few more individually named minor markings' sentence. Updated docs/editorial-backlog.md item 23 to published status (72 -> 73 blog posts), keeping the prior superseded West/Fincham-based note for history, and recorded the full claim-level evidence map and required SOURCE_SENSITIVE preflight disposition in docs/source-verification-log.md ('Pass 20').
verification: npm run audit:claim-risk -- src/content/blog/beginner/rascettes-palmistry.md (1 genuine finding: opening sentence's 'most hands show one or more' was an unsupported prevalence claim not grounded in the evidence note, which supports only Benham's own 'sometimes three, sometimes one' observation; corrected to a plain observational instruction before publishing. 5 residual flags on idiomatic 'most'/'many' usage -- e.g. 'most directly on point,' 'most defensible approach,' 'how many lines' -- manually reviewed and confirmed to be false positives, not prevalence/consensus claims about palmistry)
npm run build (118 pages built, including /blog/beginner/rascettes-palmistry/, clean)
npm run content-audit (73 blog posts, 25 lessons valid; editorial-backlog.md's Published marker matches the actual collection count)
npm run audit:all (links incl. orphan check, images, schema, indexability, accessibility all pass)

Manual review of the final article against the task packet's prohibited-scope list: no medical diagnosis or health claim presented as fact, no lifespan prediction presented as valid, no prevalence/statistical claim about bracelet count, no automatic bracelet-to-outcome scheme, no West/Fincham/commercial-source citation, no invented combination with other palm features, no vague anonymous authority, no geometry/count norm beyond the evidence note
Manual verification that every historical claim in the article traces to .ai-ops/evidence/PP-RELAY-058-benham-rascettes-boundary.md and is attributed to Benham by name
